name: Ema
summary: Ema develops AI-agent software designed to automate multi-step enterprise workflows across functions including HR, IT, and finance.
overview: Ema builds enterprise AI agents intended to work across a company’s existing software applications.

facts.label: Latest disclosed financing

bull_case: A platform that can automate workflows across HR, IT, finance, and other systems could become a durable layer in the enterprise software stack.
bear_case: Enterprise AI is crowded, and long sales cycles, security reviews, and incumbent platforms can limit adoption and pricing power.
directory_notes: Watch customer expansion, retention, and evidence of repeatable deployment.

company: Ema builds AI agents that enterprises can deploy across their existing software applications. Its platform includes pre-built agents and a workflow engine intended for functions such as HR, IT, finance, sales, and customer support.

The company says its technology combines multiple models and integrations so customers can configure agents around their own systems and data. Its investment case depends on whether those deployments become recurring operational software rather than short-lived AI experiments.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Ema is a useful read-through on the private-market race to make AI agents part of everyday enterprise operations. A durable winner in this category would need to prove security, reliability, integration depth, and measurable returns across established software stacks.

changed.text: Ema expanded its platform for building and deploying enterprise AI agents.
Raised a $77M Series B led by Creaegis, with Accel, S32, and Prosus increasing their investments.

takeaways: The Series B brings Ema's reported total funding to $140M, but the company did not disclose an exact valuation.
Its opportunity is broad because enterprise workflows span many systems, but broad platforms must prove clear ownership of the customer relationship.
Security, governance, and repeatable deployment matter as much as model capability for enterprise adoption.
Large software platforms and other AI-agent vendors can compete for the same workflow budgets.
